title: The Great Wall Isn't 2,000 Years Old — It's Ming | China Travel Expert
description:
Here's the twist most visitors miss: the Great Wall you picture — the brick-and-stone one snaking over the hills near Beijing — isn't 2,000 years old. It's Ming.

Qin Shi Huang's wall (around 221 BC) was mostly rammed earth, and most of it has crumbled away. The grand stone-and-brick wall tourists actually climb was built and rebuilt by the Ming dynasty after 1368 — roughly 600 years old, not 2,200. Different wall, different century.

★ Expert Tip: if you want the oldest-FEELING experience, skip the fully rebuilt tourist steps and visit a wild, unrestored Ming stretch (go with a guide — it's steep and crumbling).
